items.definition: The liquid water inside a fruit.
items.example: I squeeze some lime juice over the fruit.

items.definition: To make something cold so it tastes fresh.
items.example: We chill the salad in the fridge for one hour.

items.definition: A top with a collar that you wear over your body, on its own or under a jacket.
items.example: My school shirt has a blue collar.

items.definition: Clothes you wear on your legs, one piece for each leg.
items.example: I put on my trousers before my socks.

items.definition: Soft cloth you wear on your feet, inside your shoes.
items.example: These socks are too big for me.

items.definition: Hard things you wear on your feet. One is for the left foot and one for the right.
items.example: I put on my shoes by the door.

items.definition: A thicker top you wear over your shirt when it is cold or wet.
items.example: I wear a jacket when it is cold in the morning.

items.definition: The part of the day from when you wake up until lunchtime.
items.example: In the morning I drink a glass of milk.

items.definition: The middle of the day, around twelve o'clock. It is also called midday.
items.example: We eat lunch at noon.

items.definition: The part of the day after the afternoon. The light gets soft and people come home.
items.example: Good evening, Mum.

items.definition: The woman who looks after you and lives with you.
items.example: My mother works at a shop in the market.

items.definition: A small bowl with a handle. We use it for soup, rice and porridge.
items.example: Can I have a spoon for my soup?

items.definition: A tool with a handle and sharp points. We use it for food in small pieces.
items.example: I eat the fish with a fork.

items.definition: A deep round dish. Soup, cereal and rice porridge go in a bowl.
items.example: There is one bowl of noodles on the table.

items.definition: The cold box in the kitchen. It keeps food fresh for a day or two.
items.example: The eggs are in the fridge.

items.definition: A tall box with doors. Dry food and clean dishes are kept inside it.
items.example: The clean cups are in the cupboard.

items.definition: One of the ways your body finds out about the world. You have five main ones.
items.example: Smell is a sense that helps you find food.

items.definition: The screen at the back of your eye. Light lands on it and the picture begins.
items.example: The picture forms on the retina.

items.definition: The nerve that carries the picture from your eye to your brain.
items.example: The optic nerve carries the picture along to the brain.

items.definition: The little spiral inside your ear that turns vibrations into nerve signals.
items.example: The cochlea changes the movement of your eardrum into signals.

items.definition: The tiny bumps on your tongue that pick out sweet, salty, sour and bitter.
items.example: Taste buds tell you that the mango is sweet.

items.definition: The cable that carries messages inside your body, from the senses to the brain and back again.
items.example: A nerve carries the message from your finger to your brain.

items.definition: The light that comes from the Sun. It looks white, but it holds all the colours of the rainbow.
items.example: Sunlight is white until rain or mist splits it into colours.

items.definition: One thin path of light, like a single beam of sunshine through a gap in the clouds.
items.example: A ray of light fell right onto my book.

items.definition: When light bounces off tiny bits in the air and spreads out in all directions.
items.example: Scattering is the reason the whole sky is blue.

items.definition: The layer of air around Earth. It is thin, but it scatters the light and keeps us warm.
items.example: The atmosphere is the air around us, going up higher and higher.

items.definition: The daily rhythm inside you that tells you when to be awake and when to be sleepy.
items.example: My body clock wakes me up before the alarm.

items.definition: The story your brain makes while you sleep. Some people remember them, most do not.
items.example: I had a strange dream about a talking bicycle.

items.definition: The chemical your body makes in the evening when the light fades, to tell you it is time for bed.
items.example: Melatonin rises when the sun goes down.

items.definition: A baby fox, wolf or bear. A cub is small and still needs looking after.
items.example: The cub sat down and shook the leaves off his fur.

items.definition: Thorny branches that grow together and hold on tightly to whatever touches them.
items.example: Rusty's leg was caught in the brambles.

items.definition: A thick, tangled mass of bushes. You cannot see far into a thicket.
items.example: A small voice came out of the thicket.

items.definition: To attend to sound.
items.example: Treat a listen block as a playlist, not one clip.

items.definition: A rope net. It is strong and light, and it can hold a big animal.
items.example: The hunter threw a net over Leo.

items.definition: To bite something again and again until it breaks.
items.example: Mimi gnawed the rope until it broke.

items.definition: The deep loud sound a lion makes. It travels a long way.
items.example: Leo's roar woke the whole meadow.

items.definition: A kind thing you do for someone. You can do it without being paid back at once.
items.example: Mimi did Leo a favour that night.

items.definition: The small happy sound an animal makes when it feels comfortable.
items.example: Mimi purred when Leo lay down to sleep.

items.definition: A baby plant that has just come out of the soil. Very small, very green.
items.example: A green sprout appeared above the soil.

items.definition: The soft earth where plants grow. It holds water and food for the roots.
items.example: The seed fell into the soft brown soil.
